list.name: Changes
list.comment:
test(taskmaster): add unit tests for TaskService with JUnit 5 and Mockito
Why: TaskService had no tests — correctness could only be verified manually via Postman, which is slow, error-prone and not repeatable in CI Trigger: any change to mapping logic or repository delegation would go undetected until manual re-testing New behaviour: three isolated unit tests cover getAllTasks (DTO mapping), createTask (save delegation) and deleteTask (deleteById delegation) — TaskRepository is mocked, no database required, tests run in milliseconds

task.summary:
"docs: add CLAUDE.md with project context and mentor guidelines
Establishes single source of truth for AI-assisted sessions. Contains Golden Standard, mentor protocol, architecture overview, current status, known technical debt, and interview talking points."

docs: update README and CLAUDE.md with Phase 3.5 roadmap and session progress
- README: Phase 3 completions marked, Phase 3.5 (SOLID + GoF Patterns) added as new planned module, architecture diagram updated, Taskmaster portfolio entry added - CLAUDE.md: Task.java fix marked done, PoECharacter set as next task, Phase 3.5 learning plan with SOLID analogies and GoF priority table added, interview talking points expanded with Wither Pattern and @Data antipattern

refactor: migrate PoECharacter to Record and decouple initialization
Why the old code was problematic: The PoECharacter was a mutable class, making it risky to use in collections like HashMaps. Additionally, seed data was being initialized directly in the controller's constructor, which violated Spring's dependency injection principles and made unit testing difficult.
Trigger scenario: Any update to character stats could potentially corrupt data structures, and starting the application or running tests would trigger hardcoded business logic during the bean instantiation phase.
New behaviour: PoECharacter is now an immutable Java Record using the wither-pattern for state transitions. Data initialization has been moved to a dedicated DataInitializer using CommandLineRunner, ensuring a clean separation of concerns and a safer, thread-safe data model.

feat(taskmaster): implement TaskService and TaskController with CRUD endpoints
No prior implementation existed for task persistence or REST access. Completing the full Spring layer chain requires both Service and Controller. New behaviour: GET /tasks returns all tasks from H2, POST /tasks persists a new task via JPA, DELETE /tasks/{id} removes a task by id. Full chain Controller -> Service -> Repository -> Database is now functional.
